subject.title: feat(macos): Quick Chat power features — voice dictation, paste-to-app, model/reasoning control

question: Should Quick Chat permanently own this combined dictation, cross-app paste, and session-model-control feature set, including a session-persistent model selection from a transient nonactivating panel?
rationale: The patch introduces several new user-facing workflows and writes session model state; correctness repair alone cannot establish the intended product boundary or persistence policy.

options.title: Sponsor the scoped feature set
options.body: Keep the three Quick Chat capabilities together, require the paste-identity repair and native proof, and explicitly accept session-scoped model selection.

options.title: Split by product boundary
options.body: Land only the independently approved Quick Chat capabilities and move the remaining workflow or persistence decision to narrower follow-up work.

options.title: Pause the direction
options.body: Defer these power features until Quick Chat interaction and session-state ownership are explicitly designed.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the scoped feature set
recommendation.body: Keep the three Quick Chat capabilities together, require the paste-identity repair and native proof, and explicitly accept session-scoped model selection.

likelyOwner.reason: The assigned contributor authored the concrete Quick Chat implementation and is the closest available routing candidate in the supplied history.
